summary: Load a model and keep it (pinned) in the application's open pipeline: it stays on the card until it is unloaded (`/api/models/{key}/unload`), the pipeline closes or is lost, or the server stops - the idle sweep never takes it off, and no other model's load takes it off to make room. It loads beside the models already up: one load at a time, and never two of one model - a model already up is kept as it is. When it does not fit beside them, the models loaded on demand for jobs, and not answering one, come off first, the one used longest ago first; then the card source says whether it fits. The answer comes at once unless it is asked to wait: `?wait_s=N`, a plain number of seconds from 0 to 60, holds it until the model answers its health check, or its load fails, or N seconds have passed, whichever comes first - an application knows the moment its model is ready without asking again and again - and a wait on a server that stops is answered at once. The answer says where the model stands - `waiting` for the card, `loading`, `up` with its load's id, or `failed` with why - and the pipeline it is kept in. Refused `no_pipeline` when no pipeline of the application's is open (the queue's own, for its work, keeps no model), `too_many_models` when the pipeline keeps as many models as the runner keeps on the card at once, `stopping` when the server is stopping, and `bad_wait` for any other `wait_s`.
